chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Buck and Bubbles as pioneers; Bert Williams and the Ziegfeld Follies
summary: He says black performers got on big stages gradually, that Bert Williams was the first Negro in the Follies, and that dirty gags were unthinkable then.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No, they weren't, there were no performers on the stage, man. Are you kiddin'. You're talking at the time that the only person, negro on the stage at that time was like Bert Williams and -- what's the name of that act --
No, no -- there was another act, but I can't think of the name of it.

No, no -- who were they -- what's the name of that act -- it's a team, I can't think of the name of it. Anyway, see, the thing that you're forgetting that Buck and Bubbles are the pioneers for the negroes' publicity, negroes playing on the stages throughout the United States. You forget that point, dontcha. You don't realize there weren't no negroes in nothing, they got 'em anyhow but they didn't

get 'em all of a sudden -- gradually. You didn't go to the Palace Theater in those days 'cause you wanted to go in there, they got in there gradually. But you had to be somebody to get in there. That is in the world of entertainment. Not because your name was Ralph Bunche or what's his name -- I'm trying to think of his name -- Brooks -- Ralph Bunch and what's his name (Ed) Brooks.

He was the first negro in the Ziegfeld Follies, the only white show we had at that time. You see the big difference that is? Why didn't they have negroes in the Ziegfeld Follies before then? Why didn't they have them in there since then? We were the first ones after that. Are you following what I'm trying to say? Now in this era, that's back before your time -- way back before your time -- that's what I'm trying to tell you, that they didn't have no such guys doing, talking
dirty gags on no doggone stage. A negro couldn't get in the theater to tell -- couldn't get on the stage. (Inaudible) I just told you that.

So I'm in that era, before your time so you can't pull this time back to that time, what they're doing today. 'Cause they're doing more today against everything than anything I've ever seen and you ain't never seen it either. When did you ever see a 2¢ stamp go up to 15¢? When did you ever see the high cost of living as it is? When? When?
